note: STD-609 PR 1. Executable form of the machine-derivable vectors of protocol-node-vectors.json. Each row edits fixtures/protocol-node-base.json with RFC 6902 operations and states the typed outcome. 'later' lists vectors a following pull request carries; 'pending' lists vectors whose outcome the spec text leaves open. Reproducibility: protocol-node-base.json and this manifest are the source of truth and are edited by patch only; there is no generator. The test recomputes every edited protocol node's dependencies from its body references, so a hand edit cannot be masked by a graph-stage refusal. A row states the first defect in reader order only (FR-464 'Reader order'); later defects are masked by design. The 26 Q-LAYOUT vectors stay pending: schema.json defines ProtocolControlApplication but references it nowhere, and referencing it from the ProtocolNode body rule makes the base package itself fail at the parallel, choice and protocol-clause nodes, so no first schema error path exists for them until the schema is fixed in its own pull request.

deviations: Model types M::OrderView, M::OrderBook, M::Payment and M::Shipment are source-local opaque model nodes; M::OrderStarted, M::ChargeRequest, M::Receipt, M::ShipResult and M::RefundAttempt are source-local records with the one integer or Boolean field the base reads.
ShipmentOwner is the selected acme/orders relationship Order-order-Order; the base lists it in relationships and no control reads it.
Constraints other than 'sent.order = order', 'got.order = order' and 'closed.order = order' are the Boolean literal true (the TC-946 source writes { true } for most).
The compensation template Refund has no registration or activation captures, a literal-true trigger guard, retry relation and recovery predicate, and within [0, 30].
The terminal-less spellings of the source ('terminal any', 'scheduling adversarial') are present as in the prose base.

IR quire-contract-ir cf7396b4 accepts no temporal_bindings row for a compensation node (FR-322-AC-305); the base carries the row the spec requires, and admission by that reader was checked with the refund-clock row removed.

reader_order: When a row names no node, the first offending node is the lowest node-id (FR-322 ascending structural key order, which puts the clause Example::OrderFlow before its members) among the nodes the refusal's step visits; steps run in FR-464 'Reader order'. A row asserts only the first defect in reader order; later defects are masked by design.

loci.rule: locus is the JSON pointer of the first offending node or entry in reader order; 'at the node' is /semantic_graph/nodes/{i}, 'at the target' is the pointer of the reference term that names the target, and a graph-stage dependency defect is /semantic_graph/nodes/{i}/dependencies (FR-322-AC-96).
loci.wire: for malformed_wire the locus is the instance path of the first error of the repository's V2 schema validator (schema.json, jsonschema crate 0.55.0) on the edited package;
loci.no_package_location: a refusal with no package location uses the FR-096 locus convention of its stage.
loci.granularity: The locus is the node pointer /semantic_graph/nodes/{i} unless the vector names a target or a field (a reference term, a count, a value), as C10, CP11 and PA4 do; the field-level pointer of a node-level refusal is recorded in document_pointer (FR-322-AC-152). locus_basis records per row which of these applied.
